questions.learningObjective: determine concentration from ion-selective electrode potential
questions.stem: In the blind standard dilution exercise below, a technician notes the observed value. An ion-selective electrode with slope 59.16 mV per decade reads 37.3 mV lower for an unknown than for a 4.83e-3 M standard. What is the unknown concentration?

options.misconception: treats the potential ratio as a concentration multiplier
ignores the potential difference and reports the standard concentration
applies the potential shift in the wrong direction

questions.explanation: A 37.3 mV drop at 59.16 mV per decade is 37.3/59.16 = 0.63 decades. For a cation a lower potential means lower concentration, so c = 0.00483 x 10^(-0.63) = 1.13e-3 M. Reversing the sign would increase the concentration instead.
questions.hint: A decade is 59.16 mV for a monovalent ion.
